papers.title: Automatic partition identities
papers.abstract: We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected. As an application, we prove the three-row, level-two case of Primc's conjecture, which equates counts of coloured partitions subject to local multiplicity conditions with counts of coloured partitions whose parts lie in prescribed residue classes modulo eight.

papers.title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
papers.comments: 15 pages. An AI-assisted Lean development formalizes the deductions in the paper, conditional on eight explicitly documented families of external results. The development is available at this https URL
papers.abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(\kappa>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-\kappa}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.

papers.title: Optimal no-feedback card guessing after a fixed number of riffle shuffles
papers.abstract: An ordered deck of $n$ cards is subjected to $k$ independent Gilbert--Shannon--Reeds riffle shuffles. A player then guesses each card without feedback, with repeated guesses allowed. For every fixed $k\ge1$, we prove that, once $n$ is sufficiently large, an optimal guess at position $i$ in the top half of the deck is $\lfloor i/2^k\rfloor+1$; the bottom-half strategy is obtained by reflection. We also show that the optimal expected number of correct guesses is $2\sqrt{n/((2^k-1)\pi)}+O_k(1)$. Our starting point is the result of our earlier work that the label at each position is distributed as an equally weighted mixture of $2^k$ components, each a shifted sum of two independent binomial random variables (a Poisson-binomial distribution). The proof of the optimal strategy combines three ingredients: a uniform concentration estimate that separates the mixture components, exact binomial inequalities that control the gaps between competing peaks, and a coefficient comparison that resolves modal ties. The expected-score asymptotic is proved independently of the strategy, using only the peak heights of the mixture components.

papers.title: Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube
papers.abstract: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite, non-empty set not contained in any translate of a hyperplane. We show that there exists a subset $S \subseteq A$ such that $d \ll |S| \ll d$ and \[E(A,S) := |\{(a_1,a_2,s_1,s_2)\in A\times A\times S\times S:a_1+s_1=a_2+s_2\}|\ll\lvert A\rvert\lvert S\rvert.\] This can be interpreted as a robust, analytic generalisation of the classical Freiman's lemma, and recovers Freiman's lemma up to a constant multiplicative factor. In the process of proving this result, we also show that for any integer $1 \leq m \leq d$ and any set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A| \leq \binom{d}{m}$, one has \[ E(A, B) \leq 4(m + 1/m) |A||B|,\] where $B$ is the canonical basis of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. This gives new estimates for multiplicative energies between finite sets of primes and arbitrary subsets of positive integers, improving a previous result of Shkredov. Using related ideas, we also prove new bounds for an edge-isoperimetric problem for certain graphs on the boolean cube, improving an earlier result of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky. We give two different proofs of the first result described in this abstract and three different proofs of the second one.

papers.title: Odd-ordered Cayley graphs satisfy Erdős--Gyárfás
papers.abstract: Erdős and Gyárfás conjectured that every graph with minimum degree at least three contains a power-of-two-length cycle. We prove every Cayley graph of odd order satisfies the conjecture. As a corollary, we find that Cayley graphs of finite nilpotent groups satisfy the conjecture as well.

papers.title: Uniform asymptotics for the Kleitman-West problem
papers.abstract: Two distinct $r$-element sets are adjacent if their intersection has size $r-1$. The Kleitman-West problem, equivalently formulated as the edge-isoperimetric problem on the Johnson graph $J(n,r)$, asks for the maximum number $M_r(n,m)$ of unordered adjacent pairs in a family of $m$ $r$-element subsets of an $n$-element set, and for the families attaining this maximum. For every fixed integer $r\ge2$, we determine this maximum asymptotically as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over the entire range of family sizes. Specifically, for each integer $1\le j\le r$, define $F_j(p)=\max\{p^{1+1/j},\,2p-1+(1-p)^{1+1/j}\}$ for $0\le p\le1$, and $G_j(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor+F_j(x-\lfloor x\rfloor)$ for $x\ge0$. With \[ P_r(n,m)=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{n^{j+1}}{2(j-1)!}G_j\!\left(\frac{j!m}{n^j}\right)-\frac{r(r-1)}4mn-\frac m2, \] we prove that \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{2\le m\le\binom nr}\left|\frac{M_r(n,m)}{P_r(n,m)}-1\right|=0. \] The remaining cases satisfy $M_r(n,0)=M_r(n,1)=0$. The proof first establishes the asymptotic formula for dense families using a sharp inequality for bounded random variables, with equality attained by a random variable taking at most two values. To extend the result uniformly to all family sizes, we extract groups of sets sharing a fixed subset, apply the dense estimates after deleting that subset, and control the adjacent pairs not contained in any one group.

papers.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
papers.comments: Code, computer certificates and Lean 4 formal proofs: this https URL and this https URL
papers.abstract: Using the bisection bound of Monien and Preis, Fomin and Høie proved in 2006 that every graph of maximum degree 3 on $n$ vertices has pathwidth at most $n/6+o(n)$. We prove that the pathwidth, bisection width and cutwidth of these graphs are at most $c_3 n+o(n)$, where $c_3=\frac{3}{4\pi}\arccos\frac56\approx0.1398$. For bisection width this improves the bound $n/6+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis (2006) and extends to all such graphs the bound that Lichev and Mitsche (2023) obtained for random cubic graphs. For maximum degree 4, we prove that bisection width and cutwidth are at most $n/3+o(n)$, improving the bound $2n/5+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis for 4-regular graphs, and that pathwidth is at most $0.2458n$, improving the bound $n/3$ of Fomin, Gaspers, Saurabh and Stepanov (2009). We show that every graph with $m$ edges has pathwidth at most $7m/48+o(n)$, improving the bound $13m/75$ of Scott and Sorkin (2007), and we give further bounds of the form $\sum_{d\ge3}a_d n_d+o(n)$ with $a_d<1$, where $n_d$ is the number of vertices of degree $d$. The path decompositions, and linear orderings of the stated cutwidth, can be computed in polynomial time. Instead of deriving pathwidth bounds from bisection width, we give each vertex a Gaussian label, a weighted sum of independent standard normal variables over a ball around it, and sweep a threshold through the labels; the bags are frontiers, the vertices above the threshold with a neighbor below it. We bound the probability that a vertex lies in a frontier by comparison with an explicit Gaussian model of a vertex and its neighbors. Faster exact algorithms follow: for feedback vertex set and the traveling salesperson problem on graphs of bounded maximum or average degree, and on general graphs for minimum weight dominating set (by branching until the instance is sparse), Max 2-CSP and counting subgraphs with $k$ edges (by the bound in $m$).

papers.title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
papers.abstract: We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.

papers.title: Supercritical level-set percolation on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We continue the study of bond percolation on finite graphs induced by the level-sets of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the associated metric graph. In our previous work Goswami and Pal (2026), we analyzed the critical and near-critical behavior of this model on uniform expanders, focusing on the volume of the largest cluster. In the present paper, we investigate the size of the second largest cluster in the supercritical regime --- the phase where one expects a unique giant component. We prove that the second largest cluster is at most of logarithmic order with high probability. The estimates hold uniformly over deterministic graphs with a bounded maximum degree and a spectral gap bounded away from zero. In particular, we do not require any assumption regarding regularity, girth or local geometry. This picture is substantially different from Bernoulli percolation, where the second largest supercritical cluster can have polynomial volume under identical hypotheses. The proof relies on expansion properties of the underlying graph and the Dirichlet martingale framework developed in Goswami and Pal (2026).

papers.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
papers.abstract: Jaeger conjectured that, for every positive integer $p$, every $4p$-edge-connected graph admits an orientation with congruent indegree and outdegree modulo $2p+1$. We prove a stronger probabilistic counterpart: a uniformly random simple $(4p+1)$-regular graph has a strongly connected orientation with all outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$ with probability tending to one as its even order grows. More generally, for every fixed odd $d\ge9$, there is $\varepsilon_d>0$ such that its circular flow number is less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ with probability tending to one. We give explicit margins at the small degrees and prove the bound $91/33$ at degree seven, answering a fixed-upper-bound question of Li and Li. Gaps below $3$ at degree five and below $8/3$ at degree seven remain open. A uniform estimate for dense bisections also gives short intervals above the Li--Li maximum-bisection lower bound. Finally, we prove the one-unit bisection-gap conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis: at every fixed degree $d\ge3$, the typical minimum parameter for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the threshold forced by the maximum bisection by at most one.

papers.title: On the number of tiles in $[n]^d$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{T}(n,d)$ denote the set of subsets of $[n]^d$ that tile $\mathbb Z^d$ by translations, and write $T(n,d)=|\mathcal{T}(n,d)|$. We show that almost every tile in $\mathcal{T}(n,1)$ tiles $\mathbb{Z}$ by an arithmetic progression, thus determining $T(n,1)$ asymptotically. In higher dimensions, we prove that $T(n,d)=O_d\!\left(n^{C_d}3^{n^d/3}\right)$, confirming a conjecture of Benjamini, Kozma and Tzalik. In the other direction, we prove that $T(n,d)\geq (1-o(1))n^{\binom d2}3^{n^d/3}$ when $3\mid n$. This shows one cannot take $C_d=d-1$ for $d\geq 3$, answering a question due to the same authors negatively. Finally, we also obtain nearly tight bounds in dimension two. Our upper bounds rely on a new observation realising tiles as maximal independent sets in truncated Cayley graphs.

papers.title: Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ with nonnegative edge weights, let $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)$ denote the maximum total weight of a cut and let $w(G)$ denote the total edge weight. We prove that every edge-weighted triangle-free subcubic graph satisfies $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)\geq \frac{15}{19}w(G)$, improving the bound of $\frac{8}{11}$ due to Gutin and Yeo. For subcubic graphs of odd girth at least seven and nine, we strengthen this bound to $\frac{47}{59}w(G)$ and $\frac45w(G)$, respectively, establishing the conjecture of Gutin and Yeo for graphs of odd girth at least nine. Our proofs combine structural properties of vertex partitions with randomized cut constructions and convex combinations of the resulting bounds.

papers.title: Binary Codes with a Forbidden Distance
papers.abstract: The maximum size of a t-intersecting code in the set of words of length n over an alphabet of size m, a problem posed by Frankl and Füredi, was determined independently by Ahlswede and Khachatrian and by Frankl and Tokushige. Extending this result to the forbidden-intersection setting, Keevash, Lifshitz, Long and Minzer proved that, for m greater than two and n sufficiently large in terms of t, (t minus one)-avoiding codes have the same maximum size and the same extremal ball constructions as t-intersecting codes. They also raised the binary case. Here, t-intersecting requires every two distinct words to agree in at least t coordinates, while (t minus one)-avoiding forbids agreement in exactly t minus one coordinates. We solve the binary case for all t at least three and n at least the square of the sum of t and one. If the forbidden Hamming distance n minus t plus one is odd, the maximum size of a (t minus one)-avoiding code strictly exceeds the maximum t-intersecting size. If it is even, the two maxima coincide, but their extremal families differ: some maximum (t minus one)-avoiding codes are not t-intersecting. We also determine all maximum avoiding codes in the even case. For odd forbidden distances, weight parity and a fixed-point-free pairing determine the maximum, while the diameter theorem gives the comparison with t-intersecting codes. For even forbidden distances, parity splitting and coordinate deletion reduce the problem to avoiding two consecutive distances. Connected components, disjoint neighbourhoods, and Harper's vertex-isoperimetric theorem yield the upper bound, which is attained by a t-intersecting construction. The diameter theorem then determines the extremal structure, and elementary binomial estimates give the stated parameter range.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
papers.abstract: We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip. The folklore happy edge conjecture suggests that any edge shared by both the initial and the target tree (a happy edge) is never flipped in a shortest flip sequence. This conjecture was computationally verified for up to 10 points in convex position. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture both on general point sets and on point sets in convex position by providing two counterexamples on $16$ and $30$ points, respectively. The counterexample for point sets in general position also holds for compatible flips, while the happy edge property holds for compatible flips in convex point sets as shown by Aichholzer, Dorfer, and Vogtenhuber [GD 2025].

papers.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
papers.abstract: A tester decides whether a graph has a property or is far from having it. A distance estimator asks for more: it must approximately determine how many edges need to be changed. A property is said to be testable if there is a tester with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order for each conceivable distance. Similarly, if a property admits an estimator with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order, it is said to be estimable. Fischer and Newman proved that, in the dense graph model, every testable property is also estimable. We show that the passage from testing to estimation requires only a polynomial increase in query complexity. This resolves a long-standing open problem in property testing, previously tackled by Fiat and Ron, by Hoppen, Kohayakawa, Lang, Lefmann, and Stagni, and by Gishboliner, Kushnir, and Shapira.

papers.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erdős--Sós $(9,6)$-problem
papers.abstract: Let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. It has long been conjectured that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, settling the first unsolved case of the conjecture.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
papers.abstract: Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition. Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $\sigma$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $\phi$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models \phi$ in time $f_\sigma(w,|\varphi|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.

papers.title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
papers.abstract: Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer this http URL . 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025). In this paper we prove the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem. For all positive integers $s$ and $r$, let $P(s,r)$ be the oriented path consisting of two directed paths of lengths $s$ and $r$ with a common terminal vertex, and let $Q(s,r)$ be its reverse. We show that for all $K\ge3$ and all $s,r\ge1$ with $s+r\le K$, every oriented graph $D$ with $\delta(D)\ge K$ and $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\ge K-1$ for every ordered pair of distinct vertices $(u,v)\notin A(D)$ contains both $P(s,r)$ and $Q(s,r)$. Our result is the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem, and it extends the two-block result of Chen, Hou and Zhou. The proof iterates a shift of the terminal vertex of a longest path.

papers.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the $O(N)$ Model
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on a spin system with $n$ sites and possibly infinite spin spaces. We prove local-to-global spectral-gap bounds for block Glauber dynamics. Given a symmetric, entrywise nonnegative matrix $A$ with zero diagonal and $\lambda_{\max}(A)<1$ encoding local spectral bounds for a spin system, we derive global spectral-gap bounds for block dynamics on its marginal distributions. These bounds are sharp: the Gaussian system with covariance $(I-A)^{-1}$ attains equality for every choice of disjoint blocks. Our proof extends the Bochner method through an abstract inequality for orthogonal projections on Hilbert spaces. As an application, we prove that Glauber dynamics for the $O(N)$ model, with $N\geq 2$, arbitrary external fields, and couplings of either sign, has spectral gap at least $(1-\|J_{\mathrm{abs}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}/N)/n$, where $J$ is the interaction matrix and $J_{\mathrm{abs}}=(|J_{ij}|)$. We also obtain spectral bounds for swap walks and local spectral expansion of partite simplicial complexes. For complexes formed from disjoint groups of ranks in random flags of subspaces over $\mathbb F_q$, we obtain a one-sided local spectral expansion bound of $2\sqrt q/(q+1)$. This bound is independent of the number and sizes of each group, and is nontrivial for every prime power $q$. Finally, for random forests $F$ of any finite graph with arbitrary positive edge weights, we prove that \[ \Pr(e,f\in F)\le \frac{4}{3} \Pr(e\in F)\Pr(f\in F) \] for distinct edges $e,f$, improving the factor 2 supplied by general log-concavity bounds for matroid independent sets. The argument combines our extended Bochner method with the analysis of an auxiliary real stable polynomial.

papers.title: A Low-Diameter Nash-Williams--Tutte Theorem
papers.abstract: The Nash-Williams--Tutte theorem characterizes the existence of $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees by a condition on every vertex partition. We prove that, for simple graphs, the same condition guarantees $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, each of diameter $O(n/\delta)$ and with $O((n/\delta)\log(\delta+1))$ internal vertices, where $n$ is the number of vertices and $\delta$ is the minimum degree. Both bounds hold simultaneously for every tree, with absolute implicit constants independent of $k$, and each is asymptotically optimal in general. Our proof is constructive and yields a randomized algorithm with expected running time $\tilde{O}(n^5)$. We derive applications to short edge-disjoint routes and weak linkages, small Steiner trees, and survivable networks with short paths. The joint bounds also yield low-diameter spanning Eulerian subgraphs and short tours for postman and general routing problems.

papers.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})Δ$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
papers.abstract: We show that for every $\gamma>0$ and every sufficiently large $\Delta$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has spectral gap $\Omega_\gamma(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_\gamma(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+\gamma)\Delta$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/\Delta$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $\Delta$-regular tree.

papers.title: A King for Almost Everyone
papers.abstract: A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. A vertex $v$ controls a vertex $u\neq v$ if there is a directed path of length at most two from $v$ to $u$, and a $\delta$-king is one that controls at least $\delta(n-1)$ vertices. In the query complexity model, each query reveals the orientation of an edge. Shen, Sheng and Wu [SICOMP'03] established an $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ lower bound on the deterministic query complexity of finding a $1$-king, and a non-matching upper bound of $O(n^{3/2})$. Neither bound has been improved in over two decades, despite substantial progress on variants of the problem. For $\delta$-kings with $\delta < 1$, Biswas, Jayapaul, Raman and Satti [Discrete Applied Mathematics'22] showed that $O(n^{4/3})$ queries suffice to find a $\frac12$-king. Lachish, Reidl and Trehan [FSTTCS'22] improved this guarantee to $\frac12+\frac{2}{17}$ using $\widetilde{O}(n^{4/3})$ queries, and asked whether a larger fraction could be achieved within the same query bound. We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed fraction below one: for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-king using $O(n^{4/3})$ queries. The design of our algorithm is informed by a structural analysis combining a sparse regularity lemma due to Allen, Kohayakawa, Mota and Parente [Electronic Journal of Combinatorics'14] with a new sampling argument based on a reachability theorem of Afek, Gafni and Linial [arXiv'19].

papers.title: Transfer of Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence under graph operations
papers.abstract: The Weisfeiler-Leman algorithms WL(k) for $k\ge1$ form a hierarchy of increasingly powerful tests for graph isomorphism. We study how the equivalence relations they induce on graphs transfer through a graph operation $\Phi$: for a given $k$, what level of WL-equivalence between graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ guarantees WL(k)-equivalence of graphs $\Phi(H_1)$ and $\Phi(H_2)$? We call the least such level the transfer parameter $\tau_\Phi(k)$ and determine it exactly for the line graph operation $\Phi = L$: $\tau_L(k)=2k+1$ for $k\ge2$, while $\tau_L(1)=1$. We also extend these results to the $(r,S)$-line graphs, which generalize the line graph from edges to $r$-cliques by connecting two cliques when their intersection size lies in a prescribed set $S$. For these operations we prove that $\tau_{r,S}(1)=r-1$ for every $S$ and, for certain choices of $S$, that $\tau_{r,S}(k)=rk+r-1$ for $k\ge r$, and we bound the transfer parameter in the remaining range. Our upper bounds on transfer parameters follow from a treewidth analysis of diagrammatic expansions of homomorphism counts into $\Phi(H)$ as linear combinations of homomorphism counts into $H$. The matching lower bounds combine explicit constructions of witness graphs with the homomorphism-distinguishing closedness of graphs of bounded treewidth.

papers.title: The Connectivity Threshold for Friends and Strangers graphs
papers.abstract: The concept of the Friends and Strangers graph $FS(G,H)$ associated with two graphs $G$ and $H$ was recently introduced by Defant and Kravitz and has generated significant interest. In a companion article, joint with Alon, they consider the behaviour of $FS(G,H)$ in the case where $G$ and $H$ are Erdős-Rényi random graphs, and prove that the threshold for connectivity is of the form $n^{-1/2+o(1)}$. In this paper we prove that the threshold is $n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log{n}}$, up to a multiplicative constant, answering a question from Alon, Defant and Kravitz.

papers.title: Associahedra are 12-colourable
papers.abstract: We present a proper 12-colouring for all associahedra. This gives the first constant upper bound on chromatic number for this family, and disproves a conjecture of Fabila-Monroy et al. from 2009.

papers.title: A Short Proof and Generalization of the Rainbow Cycle Theorem and Improved Bounds for Binary Even-Query LCCs
papers.abstract: A \emph{rainbow cycle} in a list-edge-colored graph is a cycle where no color appears more than once. We give a short and simple proof of a result of [ABSZZ] showing that a properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph with average degree $\Omega(\log n\log\log n)$ always contains a rainbow cycle, and generalize it to weighted graphs with edges list colored with list size at most $\ell$ and where the total weight of all edges containing a given color $i$ incident to a vertex is at most $\Delta$, showing that $\Omega_\ell(\Delta\log n\log\log n)$ average degree guarantees a rainbow cycle. Using the reduction of [AG26] and the new generalized rainbow cycle theorem, we prove that for $r\geq 3$, every binary linear $r$-query locally correctable code $E:\mathbb{F}_2^k\rightarrow \mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfies $k\leq \tilde{O}(n^{1-2/(r-1)})$ by showing a rainbow analogue of the odd $r$-LDC lower bounds of [BHKL25,JM25], closing the gap between the best known lower bounds for odd- and even-query binary linear $r$-LCCs.

papers.title: The Lovász Local Lemma Is Sharp for the Hat Guessing Number
papers.abstract: In the hat guessing game on a graph $G$, each vertex is occupied by a player wearing a hat whose color is chosen from a set of $q$ colors. Each player knows the graph and their position in it and sees only the hat colors of their neighbors. The players may agree on a strategy beforehand but must simultaneously try to guess their own hat colors without communicating. They win if at least one player guesses their own hat color correctly. The hat guessing number of $G$, denoted by $\textrm{HG}(G)$, is the largest integer $q$ for which the players have a strategy that guarantees a win for every assignment of hat colors. A direct application of the symmetric Lovász Local Lemma shows that $\textrm{HG}(G) < e\Delta$ for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta \ge 1$. We prove that this bound is asymptotically sharp: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every sufficiently large $\Delta$, there exists a graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with $\textrm{HG}(G) \ge (e - \varepsilon)\Delta$. This answers a question of Alon et al., disproves the conjecture $\textrm{HG}(G) \le 2\Delta(G)$ of Bosek et al., and improves on the construction of Latyshev and Kokhas, which achieves $\textrm{HG}(G) = 4\Delta(G)/3$. The hat guessing number thus provides a natural combinatorial problem in which the Lovász Local Lemma is asymptotically tight.

papers.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
papers.abstract: We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $\phi(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $\phi(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[ \phi(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$. As a corollary, we obtain a lower bound on the independence number of $K_r$-free graphs in terms of their degree sequence. This strengthens the bound that OpenAI proved in resolving the Ajtai-Erdős-Komlós-Szemerédi conjecture. Moreover, our argument yields a deterministic algorithm that produces the desired probability distribution in time $2^{O(r^2)}n^{O(1)}$, where \(n\) is the number of vertices and the implied constants are absolute.

papers.title: Online packing of the three largest trees
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree. Our strategy is to embed the first two trees so that their union is $2$-degenerate. We prove that the complement of every $2$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices contains every tree of order $n-2$, which guarantees the final move. The main ingredient is an embedding lemma for spiders whose center must occupy a prescribed vertex having degree at most two in the forbidden graph. We then extend this lemma to arbitrary trees by induction.

surveys.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
surveys.abstract: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive
